DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA cor. Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City www.dilg.gov.ph DILG OPINION No. 15 s. 2022 Mar 04, 2022 MR. ATANACIO LACSA, JR. Lupon Clerk MS. NENITA C. BRIONES Lupon Member Both of Barangay Pembo, Makati City Dear Mr. Lacsa and Ms. Briones: This pertains to your letter dated 18 January 2022 seeking clarification from the Department on whether you can be reappointed as Lupon Clerk and Lupon Member, respectively, in Barangay Pembo, Makati City. Per your letter, Mr. Lacsa filed his Certificate of Candidacy (COC) for Congressman in Makati City COMELEC. However, on November 8, 2021, he received a formal Notice from the COMELEC that his COC is deemed not filed for filing the same with incorrect office. On the other hand, Ms. Nenita Briones also filed her COC but withdrew the same on November 5, 2021. As a result thereof, you were reappointed by the Punong Barangay Jeline M. Olfato to your respective positions last December 2021. However, your appointments were not recognized by the Treasury Department, as the latter claimed that you can only be reappointed after one year. Hence, the herein request for clarification. It may be prudent, at the outset, to clarify the positions you held prior to your filing of your respective CoCs. This is a material information as it will determine the laws applicable. It was not clearly stated in your letter what were your positions but as can be deduced therefrom, Mr. Lacsa held a position corresponding to a Lupon Clerk since the word used vis-å-vis his appointment now was "reappointed". The prefix "re" in the word "reappointed" means that he was again appointed, hence, to the same position as before. The same term ("reappointed") was also used in the case of Ms. Briones vis- a-vis her recent appointment as Lupon Member. Having established that the positions you previously held prior to your filing of your respective CoCs were appointive positions, may we now invite your attention to the "Matino, Mahusay at Maasahan" Trunkline NO.: 8876-34-54

following provisions of law and rules and regulations: I) Section 66 of Batas Pambansa Blg. 881, otherwise known as the Omnibus Election Code of the Philippines, provides "Sec. 66. Candidates holding appointive office or positions. - Any person holding a public appointive office or position, including active members of the Armed Forces of the Philippines, and officers and employees in govemment- owned or controlled corporations, shall be considered ipso facto resigned from his office upon the filing of his certificate of candidacy. " 2) Section 30 of COMELEC Resolution No. 10717 entitled "RULES AND REGULATIONS GOVERNING: 1) POLITICAL CONVENTIONS; 2) SUBMISSION OF NOMINEES OF GROUPS OR ORGANIZATIONS PARTICIPATING UNDER THE PARTY-LIST SYSTEM OF REPRESENTATION; AND 3) FILING OF CERTIFICATES OF CANDIDACY AND NOMINATION OF AND ACCEPTANCE BY OFFICIAL CANDIDATES OF REGISTERED POLITICAL PARTIES OR COALITIONS OF POLITICAL PARTIES IN CONNECTION WITH THE MAY 9, 2022 NATIONAL AND LOCAL ELECTIONS" dated August 18, 2021, provides: "SECTION 30. Effects of Filing of Certificate of Candidacy. — a. Any person holding a public appointive office or position, including active members of the AFP, and other officers and employees in government- owned or-controlled corporations, shall be considered ipso facto resigned from the office and must vacate the same at the start of the regular office hours of the day when the aspirant filed the COC. Xxxx" The operative act that will result to the ipso facto resignation of the public appointive official is his filing of the COC. Such ipso facto resignation shall start "at the start of the regular office hours of the day when the aspirant (public appointive official) filed the COC". Now we come to the issue on whether or not you can be reappointed as Lupon Clerk and Lupon Member, respectively, within the one year prohibition period This is governed by another provision of the RA 7160 or the Local Government Code of 1991. In DILG Legal Opinion No. 23, Series of 2016, the Department opined: "Clearly, Section 941 of the Local Govemment Code of 1991 is applicable only in cases of appointment or designation of a losing candidate to any office in the Govemment or any govemment-owned or controlled corporations or in any of their subsidiaries within one year following such election. The rationale behind the one-year prohibition is the extirpation of 1 Section 94. Appointment of Elective and Appointive Local Officials; Candidates Who Lost in an Election. - (a) No elective or appointive local official shall be eligible for appointment or designation in any capacity to any public office or position during his tenure. Unless otherwise allowed by law or by the primary functions of his position, no elective or appointive local official shall hold any other office or employment in the govemment or any subdivision, agency or instrumentality thereof, including govemment-owned or controlled corporations or their subsidiaries. Page 2 of 3

the "spoils system", considering that the foregoing provisions are directed against the so-called "political lameducks". As could be gleaned from the foregoing, the prohibition on appointment refers to the losing candidate. You cannot be considered candidates because the term candidate is used to refer only to a person whose COC was accepted by the proper authorities and is voted for at our elections2. A COC that is not deemed filed and one who withdraws his COC cannot be voted for at an election, hence, cannot be considered a candidate nor a losing candidate. Accordingly, we opine that you are eligible for appointment/reappointment within the one-year prohibition period. Thus, your reappointment should be recognized. This opinion is rendered without prejudice to the contrary opinion that may be rendered by a more competent authority or courts. We hope to have assisted you accordingly. Thank you.
